sectors.note:
**TL;DR:** Market breadth remains exceptionally narrow with only 2 of 11 sectors all-green, led by sustained, dominant leadership in Energy while Communication Services breaks down to the bottom of the ranks.

Energy and Healthcare are carrying market strength, representing the only groups positive across weekly, monthly, quarterly, half-year, and YTD windows. Energy holds the top spot across all sustained timeframes alongside Technology in the upper momentum tiers, providing stability at the top even as broader participation languishes. 

Rotation beneath the surface is subdued and largely defensive or bottom-tier churn. Consumer Cyclical and Utilities managed minor rank gains despite low momentum scores, while Communication Services suffered a sharp deterioration, dropping directly into last place with near-zero momentum.

## Strength
- **Narrow leadership breadth:** Only 2 of 11 groups qualify as all-green across week, month, quarter, half, and YTD frames: Energy (0.88 momentum) and Healthcare (0.73 momentum).
- **Dominant leadership:** Energy is the sole sector exhibiting sustained strength, consistently placing in the top 3 across 1-, 3-, and 6-month horizons, while holding rank 1 YTD with a leading 0.883 momentum score.
- **Top momentum cluster:** Technology closely follows Energy in overall momentum at 0.800 (rank 2 YTD), cementing a heavy concentration of strength in Energy, Tech, and Healthcare.

## Movers & Momentum
- **Communication Services breakdown:** Dropped 2 spots over the last 5 sessions to rank 11, recording a sector-wide momentum low of 0.050.
- **Marginal low-tier gainers:** Consumer Cyclical (momentum 0.400) and Utilities (momentum 0.400) each improved by +1 spot over 5 sessions, moving to ranks 10 and 9, respectively.
- **Persistent laggards:** Real Estate (0.367 momentum, rank 8 YTD) and Basic Materials (0.417 momentum, rank 5 YTD) remain anchored in the bottom momentum tiers alongside Utilities and Consumer Cyclical.

## Divergences
- **Leadership concentration:** Market resilience relies on just two all-green sectors (Energy and Healthcare), leaving the broader complex disconnected from top-tier momentum.
- **Cyclical vs. Energy disparity:** While Energy posts a dominant 0.883 momentum score, fellow cyclicals are failing to confirm, highlighted by Consumer Cyclical's weak 0.400 momentum and rank 10 positioning.
- **Fragile all-green signals:** No valid fragile all-green early-warning signals are registered across sectors (returning NaN values).

industries.note:
**TL;DR:** Energy and travel-adjacent infrastructure hold the top momentum slots, while sharp multi-week rotations favor commercial services over deteriorating manufacturing and media groups.

Breadth remains selective, with only 20 of 144 groups qualifying as all-green across all timeframes. Traditional energy dominates the upper echelon, with Oil & Gas E&P (0.865) and Oil & Gas Drilling (0.838) leading broader momentum alongside REIT - Hotel & Motel (0.865). Sustained multi-month strength is also anchored in defensive and corporate support pockets like Oil & Gas Integrated, Medical Distribution, and Insurance - Diversified.

Capital is actively rotating into industrial and business support services, evidenced by Rental & Leasing Services gaining 26 spots (to rank 33) and Security & Protection Services climbing 20 spots (to rank 55). Conversely, manufacturing and discretionary pockets are sharply fading, led by an outright collapse in Textile Manufacturing, which plunged 119 spots to rank 141. Advertising Agencies (0.038) and Resorts & Casinos (0.085) continue to anchor the bottom of the market.

## Strength
* **Broad Energy Leadership:** Energy sub-industries capture three of the top four absolute momentum slots, led by Oil & Gas E&P (0.865 momentum, YTD rank 10), Oil & Gas Drilling (0.838 momentum, YTD rank 6), and Oil & Gas Integrated (0.828 momentum, YTD rank 5).
* **All-Green Core:** Pockets maintaining positive performance across the week, month, quarter, half, and year include REIT - Hotel & Motel (0.86 momentum), Diagnostics & Research (0.83), Marine Shipping (0.83), Railroads (0.80), and Communication Equipment (0.80).
* **Multi-Month Persistence:** Groups holding top-36 rankings across 1-, 3-, and 6-month horizons include Health Information Services, Business Equipment & Supplies, Household & Personal Products, Software - Application, and Credit Services.

## Movers & Momentum
* **Top 5-Day Gainers:** Rental & Leasing Services surged +26 spots to rank 33 (0.76 momentum), Security & Protection Services moved up +20 spots to rank 55 (0.72 momentum), and Integrated Freight & Logistics gained +18 spots to rank 48 (0.66 momentum).
* **Severe 5-Day Slips:** Textile Manufacturing dropped -119 spots to rank 141 (0.21 momentum), Metal Fabrication fell -33 spots to rank 83 (0.21 momentum), and Biotechnology declined -28 spots to rank 70 (0.49 momentum).
* **Deep Laggards:** Underperformance is heavily clustered in media, gaming, and clean energy, with Advertising Agencies (momentum 0.038, YTD rank 144), Resorts & Casinos (0.085, YTD rank 137), Broadcasting (0.093, YTD rank 136), Gambling (0.103, YTD rank 143), and Solar (0.152, YTD rank 138) trailing the broader market.

## Divergences
* **Fading High-Momentum Groups:** Healthcare and financial groups are showing early exhaustion as short-term rank slips despite elevated momentum, led by Insurance - Reinsurance (0.68 momentum, down 7 spots), Medical Distribution (0.68 momentum, down 7 spots), Healthcare Plans (0.66 momentum, down 7 spots), and Lodging (0.67 momentum, down 5 spots).
* **Emerging from Low Momentum:** Early short-term buying is lifting deeply lagged industries, with Coking Coal (+9 spots, 0.51 momentum), Paper & Paper Products (+9 spots, 0.49 momentum), Recreational Vehicles (+8 spots, 0.39 momentum), and Airlines (+7 spots, 0.48 momentum) outperforming their year-to-date baselines.
